480	Yes, so it's a privilege not only for the grooms, but also for the brides. But
481	the lighter ones.
482	But this actually recalls the experience we are now describing,
483	of you standing in the Beit HaMikdash.
484	Everyone is now making room. No sacrifices now, no
485	incense, no other tasks. There is no one else
486	who is also in a rush, reading
487	the Bikurim text just to fulfill the obligation and go
488	home. There is no such thing. Everyone is now listening
489	to what you say.
490	And that includes all the Kohanim and all the people, and even
491	the Kohen Gadol.
492	What, the Kohen Gadol? Yes, Rabbi! He too stands
493	and listens to a Jew who is now reciting the Bikurim text.
494	And of course, first of all, who is listening to you? The Holy
495	One, blessed be He. After all, you are in the Beit HaMikdash, in the House of HaShem.
496	The Holy One, blessed be He, also sets aside everything else
497	and every matter, and listens to the Jew who reads the
498	Bikurim text.
499	And so, truly, this experience that the mitzvah of Bikurim
500	gives to a Jew
501	is an experience that, as we said before, is a peak
502	moment.
503	It is impossible to describe a peak moment of holiness.
504	After all, we know that when we speak about the Jewish people as a whole,
505	what is the peak moment of holiness? That the Kohen
506	Gadol, on behalf of all Israel, on the holiest day, enters the
507	Holy of Holies
508	and there atones for the whole Jewish people. But that is the Kohen
509	Gadol in the Holy of Holies.
510	But when does every Jew experience such an experience, in the connection
511	in which he reaches HaShem and says "Vaanita veamarta
512	lifnei HaShem Elokecha"? The Rebbe connects the two things.
513	He says: on Yom Kippur it says "Lifnei HaShem tit'haru,"
514	and in the mitzvah of Bikurim it says "Lifnei HaShem Elokecha,"
515	"You shall place the Bikurim before HaShem your Elokim."
516	So how do we understand this simply, that you are purified when you
517	come to HaShem, before HaShem?
518	When you bring the Bikurim, you place them
519	before HaShem. But the Alter Rebbe explains in Likutei
520	Torah that "lifnei HaShem tit'haru" means, and primarily,
521	the main meaning is
522	"before," that is, above the Name HaVaYaH, your Elokim.
523	HaVaYaH Elokecha are holy names of the Holy One,
524	blessed be He. The holiest Name is the Name HaVaYaH, but it is
525	still a name of the Holy One, blessed be He.
526	Where is a Jew able to reach? Before the Name HaVaYaH,
527	that is, to the very essence of the Blessed One, since a Jew
528	is truly a part of Elokut from above, so when he reaches
529	the essence of the Holy One, blessed be He, he is purified, cleansed
530	of all sins, since sins do not touch and do not harm
531	the bond of a Jew with the Holy One, blessed be He.
532	In the same way, when a Jew brings the Bikurim,
533	the same words are said: "before HaShem your Elokim." That is,
534	a Jew reaches such an inner and deep experience
535	that he arrives now like the Kohen Gadol on Yom
536	Kippur, in the Holy of Holies,
537	"before HaShem your Elokim."
538	And so we understand that the mitzvah of Bikurim is
539	truly an amazing, special, extraordinary mitzvah, but
540	let us notice how many conditions this mitzvah has.
541	That is why we don't, how did we say? Not only did we not
542	merit to fulfill it ourselves, there are not even pictures.
543	And why? Because this mitzvah can be fulfilled only
544	while the Beit HaMikdash exists.
545	And even when the Beit HaMikdash exists, it can be fulfilled only
546	between Pesach and Shavuot. Only then can a Jew bring
547	and read the Bikurim text.
548	And even then, who can fulfill it? Only a Jew who has
549	an inheritance in the Land of Israel. One who lives abroad cannot
550	fulfill this mitzvah, even if amazing
551	fruits grow for him there.
552	Beyond the fact that the finest fruits grow specifically
553	in the Land, but that doesn't matter, only from the Land of Israel,
554	and only one whose fine fruits grew, because one must bring from the first fruit of the ground.
555	He is obligated.
556	And only from the seven kinds. If you have what is called an orchard
557	of mangoes or apples or peaches, very nice,
558	but from that you cannot bring Bikurim.
559	People who now have... People who don't have the Bikurim in theirs or
560	on their journey, they can't bring from someone else?
561	No, no, there are no Bikurim, it's not a basket you can
562	buy in a store.
563	A friend from around, around, yes, go around.
564	Even if there is only some of the seven kinds?
565	Even only some of the seven kinds.
566	Even if there is only some of the seven kinds, you can bring.
567	Yes, yes, absolutely, but it must be in your own inheritance.
568	If it is not yours, it has no meaning.
569	It would be good for everyone to have an inheritance.
570	Nice, of course, but what does this show us? It shows us
571	that this mitzvah has so many conditions
572	and limitations
573	that apparently it is a very, very private mitzvah,
574	very unique, but very unique, meaning
575	that it is not so common and does not belong to everyone at every
576	moment and in every time and in every situation.
577	So this brings us back to the question:
578	so why, then, does the mitzvah of Bikurim become
579	the opening
580	of the Parashah that deals with the covenant, which includes all
581	our commitment and bond with the Holy One, blessed be He,
582	through the entirety of the Torah and mitzvot, all the statutes and laws?
583	So the Rebbe explains this matter in a most
584	wonderful way, with truly depths upon depths,
585	but let us try to touch on something after we drink a little.
586	L'chaim, l'chaim, l'chaim.
587	Did they all go up in holiness dressed in white, or...?
588	I'll tell you, it is not mentioned like that. About the Kohen
589	Gadol who entered the Holy of Holies, it is written that he went up
590	in white, entered in white, took off the golden garments
591	and put on the white garment, and then entered the Holy of Holies.
592	About all the people it is not written. As we said, yes, the Rebbe says this
593	is a novelty of the Rebbe, that "lifnei HaShem tit'haru" of the Holy of
594	Holies is connected with the "lifnei HaShem Elokecha" of
595	the mitzvah of Bikurim. So surely there were Jews
596	who wore white. Whether everyone was like that, I
597	don't know, it doesn't seem to me that it is mentioned
598	in halachah, but this requires further study.
599	Nice, to see everyone in white.
